panels.description: At dawn or dusk, Baba Tau sits at the mandi-gate chai stall holding his chipped glass. Opened GODARAZ is visible in the distance beside the old cotton-press wall, its oversized z catching the light. Keep upper-left sky clear.
A distant readable view of GODARAZ shows lane 3 still crowned, the pin-setter leaning into its bicycle-chain repair and the bilingual rule board still contradictory. Keep upper-left air clear.
Baba Tau lifts his chipped glass. Behind him, Bhatner’s brick walls and canal-fed green hold the town in frame. Keep upper-left sky clear.
Inside GODARAZ, Duda sits on the lane-3 ball return and cocks his head toward the open alley and town beyond. Keep upper-left interior space clear.

items.text: The lane was crooked. The machine was doubtful. The parrot was not an umpire.
THE PARROT IS NOT AN UMPIRE.
the parrot is sometimes an umpire.
But a place may be crooked and still be a place for its time.
